observations: The operator-maintained help article states that anyone can access Internet Archive collections through archive.org and that the web archive can be searched using the Wayback Machine.
The same article states that the Archive makes collections available at no cost to researchers, historians, and scholars.
The article describes preservation as the Archive mission and public access, but it also states that content can be removed or access disabled in some circumstances.

This single inspected artifact does not specify automated-access request limits, data-volume limits, API/CDX rate limits, a quota-free automation entitlement, or a durability/availability guarantee for a specific capture or API route.

This source does not establish that the exact hosted route remains usable when every optional monthly/trial/paid quota is zero, nor does it establish absence of every richer-mode/protected-primary/manual-user execution dependency for the Phase-1 outcome path.

classification.exact_route: hosted public Wayback collection access described by the General Information help article
classification.reason: Public no-cost access is supported, but the one canonical source lacks explicit evidence for automated-access limits/quota-zero operation and durable guaranteed hosted availability. Under the hard gates, absence of those proofs keeps this exact hosted route unresolved.
classification.incremental_monetary_cost: public collection access described as no-cost, but full Phase-1 zero-cost route remains unproven
